question.text: A plank called B, with mass 2m and length l, lies on a horizontal road. A block called A, with mass m, rests on top of plank B at its left-hand edge. The block and the plank are both given the same initial rightward speed v and then move together as a system. Friction acts at two surfaces: road against plank, with coefficient 1/2, and plank against block, with coefficient 1/4. Determine the following.

parts.label: a
parts.asks: Find the time that passes before block A slides completely off plank B.

parts.label: b
parts.asks: Find how far block A and plank B each travel relative to the ground up to that moment.

conditions: A (mass m) sits at B's (mass 2m, length l) left end
B rests on a horizontal road
A and B start together with rightward speed v

figure.description: Block A rests on top of plank B, positioned at B's left-hand end; plank B in turn rests on the horizontal road below it. The plank's length, l, runs the full length of B, shown by a measurement arrow beneath it. Both A and B move together to the right with the same initial speed v; the road exerts friction against the plank (coefficient 1/2), and the plank exerts friction against the block (coefficient 1/4).

solution.approach: Check whether block and plank decelerate together; since they cannot, find each deceleration and use their relative motion to find when the block has moved l relative to the plank.

steps.text: If A and B moved together, deceleration would need 0.5mg of friction between them on A alone; but the maximum available is only μ₁mg = (1/4)mg, where μ₁ = 1/4 is the block-plank coefficient (μ₂ = 1/2 is the road-plank coefficient, M = 2m the plank mass), so A and B slide on each other.
steps.equation: required 0.5mg > available μ₁mg = 0.25mg  →  A and B move separately
steps.why_this_step: This confirms the block genuinely separates from the plank, matching the question.

steps.text: Block A is decelerated only by kinetic friction from the plank.
Plank B is decelerated by road friction (backward, on its total weight (M+m)g) and pushed forward by the reaction friction from A.
Since B decelerates faster than A, A keeps sliding forward relative to B at a relative acceleration equal to the difference of the two decelerations.
Both start with the same velocity v, so their relative velocity starts at zero; the block separates once it has moved a length l relative to the plank.
Use this time in each block's own equation of motion to get the two ground displacements.
steps.equation: s_A = vt − ½(g/4)t² = vt − 2l/3;  s_B = vt − ½(5g/8)t² = vt − 5l/3

final_answer.value: (a) t = 4√(l/3g) = √(16l/3g). (b) displacement of block A = vt − 2l/3, displacement of plank B = vt − 5l/3, with t as above

common_mistakes.text: Assuming A and B decelerate together without checking the friction needed against the friction available, missing that separation ever happens.
Using the plank's own deceleration 5g/8 as the relative deceleration instead of subtracting the block's deceleration g/4, gives the wrong t = 4√(l/5g).
